title: Understanding Logistic Regression
text: In logistic regression, the probability of the binary outcome Y given the input vector X is modeled using the logistic function. This function is defined as \( \sigma(z) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-z}} \), where \( $$z$$ $$=$$ X**{T}\beta \).

title: Interpreting the Logistic Function
text: The logistic function \( \sigma(X**{T}\beta) \) maps any real-valued number into the $$(0,1)$$ interval, which represents the probability of Y being $$1$$ given X.

title: When is \( $$P(Y=1|X)$$ > X**{T}\beta \)?
text: Consider the range of values that \( \sigma(X**{T}\beta) \) can take. Since \( \sigma(X**{T}\beta) \) is always between $$0$$ and $$1$$, think about when it might be greater than \( X**{T}\beta \).

title: Comparing \( \sigma(X**{T}\beta) \) and \( X**{T}\beta \)
text: Given that \( \sigma(X**{T}\beta) \) is always between $$0$$ and $$1$$, and \( X**{T}\beta \) can be any real number, under what conditions is \( \sigma(X**{T}\beta) > X**{T}\beta \)?
